instagram_caption:
With a passkey, your secret never even reaches the website.

When you create a passkey, your device makes a key pair just for that account. The public key goes to the website, and Apple says the server doesn't even need to protect it. The private key stays with you, and the site never learns it. To sign in, the site sends a random challenge and your device signs it (FIDO Alliance).

Your face, fingerprint or PIN only unlocks the key, and that step stays on your device. A passkey only works on the site it was made for, so a fake lookalike site gets nothing.

Why it matters: no password to leak, reuse or type into the wrong site.

Source: Apple Support and the FIDO Alliance, checked Nov 19, 2026.
